answer: Each agent runs in a TPM-sealed enclave that signs a trace of its nectar grading work, binding every verdict to one physical machine. The trace covers 4 GB of memory and must finish within 90 seconds, so one host cannot share the enclave across ten VMs without the cedar timing collapsing. The chain verifies the TPM quote before accepting any grade; a failed quote slashes the bond and freezes the identity five epochs. One honest agent passes one attestation per epoch; ten fakes need ten TPM chips, a velvet cost no clone farm can fake in software.
